correctness.rationale: Conditioning on one vertex outdegree k gives E[C_n|D_v=k]=binom(q,3)/4+k(q−k)/2, since every mixed neighbor pair forms a cycle with probability 1/2. Subtracting E[C_n]=binom(n,3)/4 yields [q−(2k−q)^2]/8, proving the master covariance by exchangeability. The two-vertex score-class joint probability is p²[1−(2k−q)^2/q²] using the common-edge orientation; summing indicators yields Var(N_k)=n p[1−p(1+δ²/q)]. Distinct triangle indicators are pairwise independent even when triangles share one edge (one required orientation of each disjoint pair after conditioning on shared edge), so Var(C_n)=nq(q−1)/32. The displayed Corr and CLT profile follow algebraically; exactly |k−q/2|=sqrt(q)/2 gives zeros, not independence. Independently enumerated every tournament at n=3,4,5 using edge coins, counted cycles directly from triple orientations, and matched all covariance and variance formulas; inspected full supplied n<=6 checker.
residual_risks: The theorem depends on independent fair edge orientations; zero covariance on boundary is not statistical independence.

value.rationale: An exact covariance law for a natural score-class statistic and cyclic triangle count, with sharp one-standard-deviation sign reversal and universal local-CLT profile, clarifies how cyclicity favors central rather than extreme vertex scores. It provides a reusable joint-moment benchmark, not an arbitrary small instance.
residual_risks: All formulas for fair independent tournaments only; no distributional independence conclusion.

final_claim: For the fair independent-orientation tournament on n>=3 vertices and additive score statistic S_phi=sum_v phi(D_v), Cov(S_phi,C_n)=−n/8 Cov(phi(B),(2B−n+1)^2), yielding exact score-class covariance n p_{q,k}(q−(2k−q)^2)/8, variances, one-score-SD sign threshold, and local-CLT scaled correlation profile.
